mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 5% over two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when this trigger is met, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in the unemployment rate below 4% for two consecutive months indicates a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately reducing corporate profit margins and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, the hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) for three consecutive months signals weakening household demand, which reduces revenue growth for consumer-facing firms and results in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS shows three consecutive monthly declines
failure_condition: If S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during triggered episodes, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly contraction in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% from the previous month, sustained for two months, indicates supply-side stress that raises input costs and dampens earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change < -0.5% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: If S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered periods, the hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous monthly increase in FEDFUNDS and a decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.3 percentage points signals a restrictive policy coinciding with labor market tightness, which amplifies the negative impact on equity valuations over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases AND UNRATE decreases by >0.3pp in the same month
regime_hint: monetary tightening with labor market stress
failure_condition: If the joint trigger occurs but S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 40% of cases, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated monthly decline in both real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) and housing starts (HOUST) by more than 2% from the previous month signals a broad-based weakening in demand, which is expected to produce negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS and HOUST both decline by >2% month-over-month
failure_condition: If S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during triggered episodes, the hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: An always-on positive correlation between payroll employment growth (PAYEMS) and S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days exists during periods of moderate economic expansion (UNRATE between 4.0% and 5.0%), reflecting confidence-driven equity gains.
failure_condition: If the correlation between PAYEMS growth and 5-day S&P 500 returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05) in this regime, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of at least 0.4% for four consecutive months signals a supply-side recovery, which boosts earnings expectations and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change >= 0.4% for four consecutive months
failure_condition: If S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.10) during triggered episodes, the hypothesis is rejected.
